verdict.rationale: Gusto's evidence shows webhooks for event notifications and an MCP server aimed at AI coding assistants (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop) for building integrations, but neither constitutes a way for an AI-native end user to configure autonomous background automations within the product itself — webhooks require custom downstream logic to be built by a developer, not a self-service automation setup. Missing for 10: no evidence of a built-in automation/workflow builder, no user-configurable triggers-and-actions system, no documentation of autonomous agent execution running independently in Gusto.
